item.description: way or means of achieving something. “Na biodh saod air sin a dheanamh.”

item.headword: chan eil miann deise aig a h-ùile mìos
item.description: used in the sense of people having different tastes.
a delicate person, always prone to illness.
someone who took the blame for anything that happened.

item.headword: beag an rud is buaine na Mac an Duine
item.description: refers to the inevitability of death.
virtues.
hate. “Nach ann agad a tha ghoidh dh’an duine sin.” [NOTES: note added by Professor Roibeard Ó Maolalaigh (RÓM): goimh?]
second-hand clothes. Not pronounced separately.
threatening. “Ghròic i orm.”
a short visit. “Thug mi fideadh a staigh aca.”

item.headword: a’ bhean gu aois ’sa fear gu bàs
item.description: refers to the limited attraction of women whereas men retain their appeal till they die!! Cha bhith Curstaidh na Mòr toilichte ris an te ud.
strapping, strong. “’S tu a bheireadh an deagh smearach gille.”
demanding good quality food. “Tha na cait againne cho roichgeil.”
beautiful.
young children. “Nach eil peathairean aice a nì an obair.”
a low moaning, complaining noise sometimes associated with young children or sick animals.
Means a deterioration or worsening in condition. “Ciamar a tha a bhò agad an diugh?” “O chan eil i ach a ’s fhior dhol an ronng.”
in a jiffy. “Thig mi mach thugad ann an craic.”
when eyes are not fully open, e.g. first thing in the morning. “Bha e an sin ’s geòsgil air.”
Bruich, bruich, bruich, Cuid a leanabh bhig, Leanabh beag a call a chèile ’sa chuid fhein a bruich. A little rhyme said whilst the child’s food was cooking.
Chaidh an comann math a dh’olaidh. – said when people fall out after being good friends.
Galair fada ’s eùg [sic] na bhun. – death after a long illness.
a ball of wool in the palm of your hand. Chan e tlàm a tha air a cuigeil. – giving the impression that you are thinking of a particular subject while your interests lie elsewhere.
Ghabhainn air do chuideachadh thu fuireach bhuam. – in other words I could do better on my own.
a nuisance.
hanging onto you or always following you. “Bha i a sìor phliotail ruim [sic].” I have heard this used more often in the sense of hobbling.
well-off, rich. “Tha iad sin gu math bearateach.”
Latha fada Fhéill Phàdruig a dh’fhòghnas dh’an duine ’s fòghnaidh an duine dha. – an expression associated with Midsummer’s day.
mushrooms.
showy on the outside but empty on inside.
Cha robh duin’ uasal gun sgall.
Che dean aithreachas mall bonn feum.
’S math a chreach a dh’fhàgas an darna leth.
